description: A small, pale earthworm, curled under a stone near the roots, glistening with moisture.
A single black carpenter ant, its carapace shiny as lacquer, crawling up the bark in an unhurried line.
A fat, reddish ant, carrying a crumb of something soft and pale, marching purposefully up the trunk.
A long, dark line of carpenter ants marching up and down the trunk, following a pheromone trail.
A small, sandy mound at the base of the tree, swarming with tiny, busy ants.
A tiny, pale green aphid, clinging to a tender shoot near the base of the trunk, drinking sap through a needle-thin mouth.
A small, iridescent beetle, its shell shifting from green to blue as it catches the light.
A large, glossy black beetle with spiny legs, clinging to the bark.
A tiny, metallic green beetle, no bigger than a grain of rice, crawling across the bark in quick, jittery movements.
A striped, reddish-brown beetle, chewing a small hole into the soft wood near the base of the trunk.
A single honeybee, resting on the bark, its legs dusted with golden pollen.
A large, fat bumblebee, crawling slowly up the trunk, its fuzzy body vibrating with a deep hum.
A small, chalky white splatter of bird droppings on the bark, already dry and crusted.
A dark, purplish splatter of bird droppings on an exposed root, still fresh and glistening.
A small, cup-shaped nest wedged into the fork of a low branch, made of twigs, moss, and soft grass.
A dense, tangled nest of dry grass and feathers, tucked into a hollow at the base of the trunk.
A collection of tiny, delicate bones — a rib, a vertebra, a hollow leg bone — bleached white and scattered in the leaf litter.
A single, fragile bird bone, hollow and light as a feather, resting on the moss.
A large, heavy leg bone, weathered grey-white, with a rough, knobby joint at one end.
A thick, curved rib bone, broad and smooth, half-buried in the dirt between two roots.
A monarch butterfly, its wings slowly opening and closing as it rests on the bark.
A tiny, pale blue butterfly, fluttering around the base of the trunk, landing briefly on a sun-warmed stone.
A small, round, wooden button, carved with a pattern of leaves. It is worn smooth.
A single, ornate brass button, tarnished green with age, resting in a crack between two roots.
A fat, fuzzy caterpillar, banded in black and orange, inching its way up the trunk.
A tiny, bright green caterpillar, nibbling a hole in a fallen leaf at the base of the tree.
A long, reddish-brown centipede, its many legs rippling as it disappears into a crack in the bark.
An empty, translucent, brown cicada shell, still clinging to the bark.
A small, tarnished copper coin, wedged into a crack in the bark. A faint impression of a leaf remains on its face.
A silver coin, half-buried in the moss at the base of the tree, a tiny star scratched into its face.
A single, ancient gold coin, its surface worn almost smooth, resting in the mud between two roots.
A tiny, brass coin with a hole punched through the center, threaded onto a dried leather cord.
A small pile of deer droppings, dark and round, at the base of the tree.
A scattering of small, dark, oblong rabbit pellets, fresh and soft.
A single, cylindrical owl pellet, made of compressed fur and tiny bones, resting at the base of the trunk.
A small, dark, tapered dropping, left by a fox. It smells faintly musky.
A small, papery, brown egg case, attached to the bark like a tiny, ridged purse.
A round, white, papery egg sac, attached to the bark by a thread of silk.
A small, brown, speckled feather, wedged into a crevice in the bark.
A single, bright yellow feather, from a warbler, lying on an exposed root.
A large, glossy, black feather, from a crow, stuck upright in the moss at the base of the tree.
A long, grey-and-white striped feather, from a hawk, resting on the leaf litter.
A large, blue-grey feather with a bold black tip, from a blue jay.
A single, soft, grey-and-white downy feather, caught in a crack in the bark.
A small, delicate fern, growing out of a damp crack at the base of the trunk.
A single, iridescent bluebottle fly, rubbing its front legs together as it rests on the bark.
A small, dark, biting fly, hovering persistently near the base of the tree.
A small, pale, shelf-like fungus growing out of the side of the trunk, its edges frilled.
A cluster of tiny, bright orange fungi, growing in a neat row along a crack in the bark.
A single, large, bracket fungus, banded in brown and cream, growing out of the trunk like a small shelf.
A single, tall, elegant, black-stemmed mushroom, growing out of the leaf litter at the base of the tree.
A cluster of pale, delicate, bell-shaped mushrooms, growing out of a mossy patch at the base of the trunk.
A large, round, white puffball, growing in the grass near the roots.
A tiny, perfectly round, blue glass bead, lying in the dirt between two roots.
A small, smooth, green piece of sea glass, worn by years of tumbling.
A small, green grasshopper, clinging to the bark with its long, spindly legs.
A large, brown, speckled grasshopper, resting on a sunny patch of bark.
A fat, pale, segmented grub, curled up in a hollow beneath a piece of loose bark.
A tiny, green inchworm, looping its way slowly up the bark.
A bright red ladybug with seven black spots, resting on the bark.
A cluster of small, orange ladybugs, huddled together in a warm crack in the bark.
A single, dry, curled oak leaf, caught in a crevice in the bark, rattling in the wind.
A fresh, green leaf, wedged into a crack in the bark, still soft and pliable.
A single, brilliant red maple leaf, resting on an exposed root.
A pale, translucent, skeletonized leaf, its fleshy parts eaten away, leaving only a delicate framework.
A tiny, perfect, bright green leaf, growing from a small sprout at the base of the tree.
A patch of pale, silvery-green lichen, crusting the bark in a ruffled pattern.
A bright orange lichen, growing in a perfect circle on the bark.
A beard-like tangle of grey-green lichen, hanging from the bark in wispy strands.
A pale, powdery blue-grey lichen, dusting the bark like fine frost.
A small, brown, striped lizard, basking motionless on a warm patch of bark.
A small, pale green praying mantis, perfectly still on the bark, its triangular head turned toward you.
A single, smooth, blue glass marble, half-buried in the dirt at the base of the tree.
A small, chipped, white marble, wedged into a crack in the roots.
A small, dark, segmented millipede, curled into a tight spiral at the base of the tree.
A thick, soft carpet of green moss, growing up the north side of the trunk.
A tiny, perfect cushion of star-shaped moss, growing in a crack in the bark.
A pale, dry, feathery moss, growing in a sun-dappled patch at the base of the tree.
A large, pale moth with powdery wings, resting motionless on the bark.
A small, brown, intricately patterned moth, its wings folded flat against the bark.
A small, rusty iron nail, driven into the bark long ago, holding a faded scrap of cloth.
A single, handmade iron nail, square-headed and rough, driven into the trunk at chest height.
A small, folded scrap of paper, tucked into a crack in the bark. It reads: 'If you're reading this, you're lost. Welcome to the club.'
A piece of birch bark, curled around a twig, with words scratched into it: 'I was here. Were you?'
A tiny, rolled-up note, tied with a single strand of grass. It reads: 'The tree behind you is watching. So am I.'
A small note, pinned to the bark with a thorn: 'Beware the squirrel with the red scarf. He is not what he seems.'
A scrap of paper, damp and wrinkled: 'I found the best climbing tree in the forest. This is not it.'
A tiny note, written in a very neat, tiny hand: 'I planted an acorn here on a Tuesday. Please water it if you remember.'
A small note, written in berry juice, now faded: 'The treasure is not under the tree. It is in the tree. But not this tree.'
A crumpled note, clearly written in a rush: 'DO NOT LOOK BEHIND YOU. Just kidding. Or am I?'
A note on a scrap of birch bark: 'I came here to find peace and quiet. I found a squirrel. Close enough.'
A tiny note, tucked into a knot: 'To whoever finds this: the answer is 42. You're welcome.'
A note on a scrap of leather: 'I traded my map for a sandwich. No regrets.'
A note, written in shaky handwriting: 'The bees are organized. Do not trust them.'
A note, written in confident, looping script: 'Whoever finds this is now legally obligated to have a wonderful day.'
A small note, folded into a paper crane, tucked into a crack in the bark. It reads: 'I folded this into a crane. It does not fly. I am disappointed.'
A note, written in a formal, old-fashioned hand: 'To Whom It May Concern: The oak trees are plotting something. Please investigate.'
A tiny scrap of paper: 'I left my hat somewhere in this forest. If you find it, please wear it for a bit. Hats get lonely.'
A note, written in a small, precise hand: 'Day 47 in the forest. The squirrels have accepted me as one of their own.'
A single, small, hard, brown nut, wedged into the bark.
A cracked, empty hazelnut shell, resting on a root.
A single, shiny, brown chestnut, resting in the moss at the base of the tree.
A small pile of acorns, carefully gathered and left at the base of the tree.
A round, hard, brown growth on the bark, about the size of a small plum, smooth and warm to the touch.
A thick, gnarled root, rising out of the ground and curling over the surface before diving back down.
A tangle of fine, hair-like roots, exposed where the soil has washed away.
A single, massive root, as thick as a man's arm, snaking across the ground away from the tree.
A hollow root, its center rotted away, forming a natural tunnel just big enough for a small animal.
A single, golden drop of sap, oozing from a crack in the bark, thick and sticky.
A long, dried trail of amber-colored sap, running down the trunk like a frozen tear.
A fresh, sticky patch of sap, oozing from a fresh wound in the bark.
A single, winged maple seed, caught in a crack in the bark, spinning in the breeze.
A tiny, hard, black seed, resting on the moss at the base of the tree.
A tiny seedling, sprouting from a crack in the bark where a bit of soil has collected.
A small seedling, pushing its way up through the leaf litter at the base of the tree.
A tiny, spiral snail shell, empty and dry, wedged into a crack in the bark.
A small, smooth, white shell, the size of a thumbnail, resting in the mud between two roots.
A single, iridescent, mother-of-pearl shell fragment, catching the light in a hundred colors.
A single, dark grey slug, glistening with slime, making its slow way up the trunk.
A large, orange-brown slug, curled up under a piece of loose bark.
A silvery, dried slug trail, tracing a wandering path across the bark.
A small, brown, striped snail, its shell spiraling perfectly, slowly climbing the trunk.
A small, green garden snake, coiled in a sunny patch at the base of the tree.
A long, translucent snakeskin, caught on a low branch and trailing down the bark.
A small, dark wolf spider, sitting motionless in a crack in the bark.
A large, hairy, brown spider, its legs spanning the width of your palm, resting on the trunk.
A small, perfect, dew-covered spiderweb, spun between two roots, glittering like a net of diamonds.
A tangled, dusty spiderweb, filling a crevice in the bark, with a dried husk of a fly caught in it.
A grey squirrel, clinging to the trunk and staring at you with bright, curious eyes.
A small, straight, dry stick, about the length of a finger, lying on an exposed root.
A long, curved walking stick, leaning against the trunk as if someone left it behind.
A forked stick, sharpened at one end, wedged into the ground beside the tree, a crudely carved 'R' on the handle.
A single, smooth, grey river stone, resting on an exposed root.
A small, flat, grey stone, wedged into a fork in the roots, worn smooth by water.
A large, flat, dark stone, half-buried at the base of the tree, warm from the sun.
A small, rough, sparkling stone, dotted with tiny crystals that catch the light.
A perfectly round, white stone, no bigger than a marble, resting in a bed of moss.
A narrow, winding, mud-covered termite trail, running up the bark like a tiny, brown vein.
A tiny, dark tick, crawling up the bark, waiting for a warm-blooded host to pass by.
A small, brown, warty toad, sitting at the base of the tree, half-hidden under a fallen leaf.
A small set of tracks, pressed into the soft earth at the base of the tree.
A single, clear deer hoofprint, pressed into the mud near the roots.
A set of tiny, delicate bird tracks, pressed into the soft mud near the base of the trunk.
A thin, dry, forked twig, wedged into a crack in the bark.
A small, fresh, green twig, snapped off and lying on an exposed root.
A single, perfectly straight twig, about a foot long, leaning against the trunk.
A single, yellow-and-black wasp, crawling slowly over the bark, its wings folded back.
A small, grey, segmented woodlouse, curled into a tight, armored ball at the base of the tree.
A long, pink earthworm, half-emerged from the soil at the base of the tree.
A small, smooth stone, glowing with a soft, steady pink light, resting in the moss between two roots. Birds are fond of them and often drop them in places like these.
A small, smooth stone, glowing with a cool, gentle blue light, half-buried in the soil at the base of the trunk. Birds are fond of them and often drop them in places like these.
A small cluster of glowstones, nested together in a hollow between roots, each pulsing softly in its own color.
A small, smooth stone, once bright, now dim and grey. A faint trace of light still lingers deep inside, like a forgotten memory.
A smooth, pale stone that grows warmer when the moon is out and cool when the sun is up. It feels alive in your palm.
A slender root that glows faintly from within, its light pulsing slowly, like a heartbeat buried in the soil.
A thick, gnarled root that hums a low, steady note when touched. The note changes with the season, never the same twice.
A strip of glowing runes carved into the trunk, warm to the touch. They shift slowly, spelling words in a language you almost recognize.
A single, glowing rune carved into the bark, pulsing gently in time with your own heartbeat.
A tiny, arched door, no bigger than your thumb, set into the base of the trunk. It is closed, and warm to the touch.
A perfect circle of small, pale mushrooms, growing in the grass at the base of the tree. The air inside the ring smells faintly of honey.
A ring of dried, blackened mushroom stumps, long dead, still marking a perfect circle in the moss. Something once happened here.
A smooth, grey stone, cool to the touch, that shows a brief, silent scene from the forest's past when you close your eyes and hold it.
A small, smooth pebble that quietly repeats the last word you spoke to it, in your own voice.
A small drift of pale, glittering dust, gathered in a hollow between roots. It shimmers faintly and feels warm.
A single, pale acorn, warm to the touch, humming a soft, wordless tune. It stops when you move away.
A root that glows like a banked ember, warm but never burning, never cooling. It lights the soil around it in soft, orange hues.
A single, frozen dewdrop that never melts, resting on a blade of grass at the base of the tree. It hums faintly when touched.
A thick, golden sap that oozes slowly from a wound in the trunk, glowing faintly and smelling of honey and warm resin.
A small, silver bell, half-buried in the soil at the base of the tree. It rings faintly when uncovered, though no one touched it.
A small pile of fine grey ash at the base of the trunk, all that remains of something that once burned.
A curled, blackened strip of bark, still smelling faintly of smoke.
A stone blackened by fire, its surface cracked from the heat. It is still slightly warm.
A single acorn, charred black on the outside, the cap burned away. The inside smells of scorched oil.
A dark, sooty stain smeared on the bark in the shape of a hand, as if someone tried to steady themselves.
A dark, hardened lump of resin, melted by fire and cooled into an odd, twisted shape.
A copper coin, warped and blackened by fire. The face is gone; only a smooth, dimpled disc remains.
A tiny fireweed seedling, sprouting from the blackened soil. Life returning to a place that burned.
A glowstone, dimmed to a deep, ember-red by fire. It never fully cools. Whatever color it once was, this is what remains.
A scrap of paper at the base of a burned tree. Only one line survives in careful handwriting: 'I came back for you. I was too late.'
A thin, twisted tube of pale glass, formed when lightning struck the sand at the base of the tree. It hums faintly.
A stone split cleanly down the middle, the inside smooth and almost polished, as if the lightning carved through it.
A small, dark stone that smells sharply of ozone and rain. It tingles slightly in your hand.
A silver coin, its surface frosted and cracked by lightning. It seems to hum when held up to the sky.
An acorn that fell during the storm. It is oddly heavy and crackles faintly when shaken.
A glass marble, clouded by heat, with a tiny branching pattern of cracks inside. It looks like a trapped lightning bolt.
A tiny bead of glass, formed in the instant of the strike. It is smooth, black, and warm.
A glowstone that was in the tree when lightning struck. It is now white-gold and fiercely bright. Birds will not touch this one. This is the form all glowstones take when the storm finds them.
A thin sliver of root, hardened and glassy from the strike, warm to the touch and humming faintly.
A jagged shard of wood, broken from the trunk where the lightning struck. One side is smooth, the other charred.
